name: A year of an Ontario company selling across Canada and abroad, filing GST34 quarterly

documents.why: The ordinary sale of a company established in Ontario to an Ontario customer: one harmonized rate, one administration, one box. 10,000 on line 101 and 1,300 on line 103.

The document this pack exists to prove: a supply made in Québec carries one code at 14.975 % and the posting splits it in two — 400.00 of GST on line 103 of the federal return and 798.00 of QST on an account this return never sees.
A purchase in the company's own province: the whole of the 13 % is an input tax credit on line 106, and the base of a purchase reaches no box because form GST34 has no input side.

A zero-rated export under Schedule VI, Part V, section 1: nothing is charged, the revenue still reaches line 101, and the seller keeps every input tax credit behind it — which is what makes a zero-rated supply different from an exempt one.

lines.name: Shipment to Buffalo, ex works Toronto

documents.why: A machine bought in Saskatchewan: of the 330.00 of tax, 150.00 is the federal 5 % and a credit on line 106, and 180.00 is provincial sales tax nobody gets back, so it is capitalised with the machine — 3,180.00 on account 1430.
The other side of a stacked tax: on a supply made in British Columbia the seller collects 250.00 for the Receiver General and 350.00 for the Province, and only the first reaches line 103.

An exemption: a residential lease of at least one month is exempt under Schedule V, Part I, section 6. No tax, and the rent still reaches line 101 — the return asks for total sales and other revenue, exempt revenue included.

lines.name: Apartment over the workshop — six months

documents.why: A purchase in Québec, where both taxes come back: 100.00 of GST on line 106 of this return and 199.50 of QST on an account whose refund is claimed from Revenu Québec on a form this pack does not carry.
Alberta: no participating province and no provincial sales tax, so the federal 5 % is the whole of it — the simplest shape a Canadian sale takes.
Equipment hired in Manitoba: 75.00 of federal tax recovered on line 106 and 105.00 of retail sales tax that is part of what the hire cost, so account 6230 carries 1,605.00 and not 1,500.00.
Nova Scotia at 14 %: the rate the province dropped a point on 1 April 2025, and the reason this pack carries five harmonized rates and not three.

An imported taxable supply under section 218: nobody charged the tax, the recipient owes it, and nothing is recovered — 200.00 is added to what the software cost and the same 200.00 is declared on line 405.
Basic groceries, zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part III: a rate of zero because Parliament set one and not because an exemption was claimed. Line 101 and no line 103.

lines.name: Staff canteen — unprepared food resold at cost

documents.why: A credit note on the January sale: line 101 and line 103 both go down, which is what the negative box factors are for, and the adjustment lands in the quarter the credit note is dated in.
Rent in Ontario, taxable at 13 % and fully recoverable: a commercial lease is not the residential lease of S5, and the two codes are what keeps them apart.
A service invoiced in Ontario at the end of the year, unpaid at the balance sheet date: it is what leaves a receivable on the closing trial balance.

payments.why: A receipt that settles its invoice to the cent, tax included.
The Québec invoice paid in full: 8,000.00 plus 400.00 of GST plus 798.00 of QST, which is how the two rates add up in cash.
A supplier paid in full, so the payables side of the year is matched too.
An export collected with no tax on it: the amount received is the invoice.
The Saskatchewan machine paid for: 3,000.00 plus 330.00, of which only 150.00 will ever come back.
The British Columbia invoice collected, provincial sales tax included — the company holds 350.00 that belongs to the Province.
A payment on account that settles nothing: an unmatched receipt is what an open-item ledger has to be able to hold.
